title: COIN game definition
description: Single source of truth for one COIN-style prototype. All printable text and diagrams are generated from a confirmed revision of this document.

status.description: final only after explicit confirmation and passing validation

supplies.description: Common supplies the print kit does not include, such as dice.

progress.description: Wizard step progress. Absent steps count as not started.

touched.description: The designer edited something in the step.

done.description: The designer marked the step done and it had no blockers.

opinionLevels.description: 1.9.0: 3 opinion levels (Support 1, Neutral 0, Opposition -1; the default) or 5 (Active Support 2 to Active Opposition -2), as the game's rules say.

links.description: Gameplay adjacency. Independent of drawing positions.

oneOf.description: Image drawn under the printed board.

href.description: A data URL or a web address.

spaceAttributes.description: Starting values of mutable space attributes, such as opinion.

pools.description: Per piece type: counts outside the board. available + outOfPlay + on-board must equal supply.

firstActor.description: Plain text: how the first actor is found from the card order and eligibility.

secondActorOptions.description: Key: first actor choice. Value: allowed choices for the second actor.

passGain.description: Resources gained on Pass, by faction id.

text.description: Plain rulebook paragraphs by section id. Generated rulebook uses these in order.

control.description: Control (1.11.0). A faction or side controls a space when its pieces there outnumber all other pieces. $space.control reads the side id, the faction id or none.

sides.description: Factions that control together, such as COIN = US + ARVN. A faction in no side controls alone.

exclude.description: Pieces that do not count toward Control.

types.description: Space types that can be controlled. Left out: every space.

events.description: Event card ids in this pile, shuffled together.

scoringPlacement.description: Positions inside the pile, 1 = top. The scoring card lands in this range.

readScope.description: What was actually read, for example a character range.

check.description: Result of checking a historical claim against its sources.

passage.description: The source passage that decided the verdict, by character position.

symbol.description: Letter or glyph printed with the color so color is never the only cue.

preset.description: Preset that supplied this faction's defaults. Informational: type stays the source of truth.

expr.description: Small expression language: literals, {var}, {op,args}. Ops: and or not eq ne gt gte lt lte add sub mul min max count adjCount sumSpaces anySpace attr factionCount canPlace canDo unmoved avail factionAvail cardCould.

step.description: Effect step. Fields per op come from src/ops.mjs.

faction.description: The enemy faction this option acts against (1.6.0). A bot whose action node picked an enemy ($target) takes the option for that faction.

piece.description: 1.9.0, needs faction: a piece type of that faction. A bot whose opponent table picked that piece takes this option and no other.

legal.description: Spaces where this option can be used (1.6.0, needs faction). When the action is used against that faction, a space must meet both the action's targets and this.

dependsOn.description: Pieces, tracks or space attributes the action needs.

targets.description: Legal space filter, evaluated per space with $space bound.

templateId.description: Archetype this action was built from. Informational only.

plainOf.description: Fingerprint of the steps when the plain text was last written. A different fingerprint marks the text as stale.

purpose.description: One line: why a player takes this action. Printed on the faction sheet.

ruleRef.description: Rulebook section, such as 3.3.1. Printed after the action name.

accompanies.description: Special Activities only: the Operations it may go with, or any.

maxSpaces.description: Special Activities only: the most spaces it may affect.

spaceText.description: Special Activities only. A phrase for the space tag on the faction sheet, such as "among 3 spaces". Printed in place of "max N spaces"; print only.

plainOf.description: Fingerprint of the steps when the plain text was last written. A different fingerprint marks the text as stale.

lasting.description: The side's effect lasts: a Momentum Event (until the next scoring card) or a Capability (for the rest of the game). The side's text states what it does; the variable card.lasting reads it.

node.description: How the bot runs the Event (schema 1.10.0): the steps of the side it plays. The table picks every space a step needs; the optional target table picks the enemy first. The override's plain text is the label.

plain.description: Plain-language rule for when the bot plays an Event.

scope.description: space: picks spaces. opponent: picks one enemy faction, read as $faction in its steps and tie-breaks.

tiebreak.description: Tie-breaks for this step only (1.7.0), as printed under one row of a GMT sheet. They replace the table tie-breaks for this step's matches.

piece.description: Opponent tables only (1.9.0): a piece type of an enemy. The step considers only that piece's owner faction; the action then runs only a choice option made for that piece.

target.description: Space tables only (1.8.0): the enemy faction this step acts against. Its filter and tie-breaks read $target, and its spaces run the action against that faction.

mode.description: first (default): only the first step with a match applies. sequence (1.7.0, the GMT reading): every step in order, each step's matches in tie-break order, until the limit.

code.description: Short code that prefixes priority table labels on the printed aid.

layout.description: Manual flowchart positions by node id. Nodes without an entry are placed automatically.

scoring.description: Choices in scoring phases. In each named phase, every step that needs a space (spaces with filter, or a choose space) picks with this table.

text.description: Printed in the scoring box of the Non-Player sheet and the bot aid.

mode.description: 1.12.0. flowchart (default): the bot runs its nodes. cards: the bot runs its nodes, and the exit $draw draws a card from its deck.

deck.description: The bot deck (1.12.0, mode cards only). order: cycle (a drawn card goes to the bottom face up, Jacquard) or shuffle (a drawn card is discarded, then the deck is shuffled, ABB). In one turn both draw the cards in order.

linked.description: One linked Special Activity, or a list tried in order: the first entry whose trigger holds and whose table finds a space runs.

target.description: An opponent table. The action picks this enemy first; its space table can read $target.

budget.description: Action nodes only (1.11.0): what the Operation may spend. share: [num, den] of Resources, rounded down; allBelow: spend all when Resources are below it; floor: keep at least this many. With share and floor, the smaller spend wins. A linked Special Activity pays from the full Resources.

parts.description: Numbered sub-actions of one Operation. Each part picks spaces with its own table and runs its own steps there. The Operation's cost is paid once per distinct space over all parts. The node is empty only when every part is empty.

noActivation.description: 1.12.0 part B, action nodes on a card side with an Activation Number: this Operation skips the roll and takes spaces up to its table's limit.

branch.description: A node id, or an exit of a card bot (1.12.0): $draw draws the next bot card; $flip turns the current bot card to its other side.

botCard.description: One card of a bot deck (1.12.0). Each side is a small flowchart with today's node kinds.

sides.description: front, then back. A card with one side cannot flip.

label.description: The side's printed letter, such as A or AA.

activation.description: 1.12.0 part B: the Activation Number of this side, a number or a formula (a track value). Before each space after the first, an action node on this side rolls 1d6; a roll at or under the number ends its Operation.
